entry.title: the Dutch East Indies was the third-largest exporter of tea (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that during the colonial period, the Dutch East Indies was the third-largest exporter of tea after the British Raj and Ceylon?

entry.content: ... that the director of Eating Out 2: Sloppy Seconds once described the film as "gaysploitation"?

entry.title: Xu Xinfu (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Xu Xinfu adapted the fictional Chinese-American detective Charlie Chan for Chinese audiences?

entry.title: Griffin–Spalding County Airport (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that large aircraft once operated on a regular basis from Griffin–Spalding County Airport despite it only having a 3,100-foot-long (940 m) runway?

entry.title: Susanne Craig (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Susanne Craig won the Pulitzer Prize for Explanatory Reporting for her reporting on Donald Trump's taxes after receiving a copy of his tax records in her mailbox?

entry.title: Hotel Marseilles (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that New York City's Hotel Marseilles, once a shelter for Holocaust survivors, later became affordable housing for the elderly?

entry.title: Anatolii Brezvin (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Anatolii Brezvin helped establish a youth hockey championship in Ukraine, and sought to open 60 ice rinks?

entry.title: Union of Assyrians (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the Union of Assyrians's mishandling of shoe-polishing stations led to violent conflicts in 1920s Moscow?
